meta.title: Theming
meta.description: The preset, the color scheme and the density, the tokens behind them, and how dark mode works.

tokens.intro: Three props decide how the schedule looks: preset is its shape, colorScheme its palette, density its spacing. They are independent — any of the twelve combinations is valid, and all of them are styled.
tokens.props: Under those three, everything is a CSS variable. tokens sets them on the root of the component, which is the smallest way to change one value without a stylesheet of your own:

dark.intro: The dark scheme is not a separate stylesheet: it is the same tokens with other values, selected by a data attribute the component sets. That means you can override the dark values the same way you override the light ones:
dark.system: colorScheme="system" follows the reader’s own setting through prefers-color-scheme, and updates when that changes. Whatever you choose, the contrast of the default preset is what the accessibility page reports.

presets.intro: A preset is the shape of the component, not its colors.
points: 'default' — what this site shows: rounder cards, a stronger level rail, more air between the rows.
'classic' — denser and flatter, for a screen that has to hold more at once.
Both work in both color schemes and all three densities, and both are covered by the visual tests.
A preset changes only what CSS can change; the structure, the names and the behavior are the same in each.
